summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma on Cytoxan, Revlimid, and Decadron, was admitted with cough, shortness of breath, and malaise. He was found to have a new left lower lobe pneumonia, acute kidney injury likely from dehydration, and a supratherapeutic INR of 4.1 that peaked at 5.7, causing metabolic encephalopathy. He was treated with IV fluids, levofloxacin initially, then switched to cefepime and later vancomycin and cefepime due to worsening pneumonia. A urinary tract infection with enterococcus was treated with ampicillin. His atrial fibrillation converted to atrial flutter, which stabilized with rate control. He received two units of blood for anemia and vitamin K with FFP for coagulopathy. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. He improved clinically, with resolving pneumonia on imaging, and was discharged home on a 14-day course of IV vancomycin and cefepime, oral azithromycin, and adjusted warfarin. Follow-up was arranged for labs, imaging, and oncology care.
problems: Multiple myeloma, without mention of having achieved remission
